# Reserve activation through successive saturated-neighbor compensation

Status: OPEN analytical candidate, hand-derived before new enumeration. Parent c31f5313486be2be25ff1d32d01b507d2de2e313 closes source escape. This campaign addresses escape to a usable absent label within a specified monotone template, not complete native reachability.

## Domain

Retain finite simple isolate-free H with source vertex-cover number three or four, positive original multiplicities a, original palette and star footprints M_v. G is a saturated subgraph; original floor on uv is a_u+a_v in G, otherwise one. All current footprints must be contained in some original star. Original protected hidden completions stay fixed; upper-four is required.

Choose a nonempty G-independent set I of donor types. Put N=N_G(I), disjoint from I. Fix any original H vertex cover C of size at most four with a_i>=2 for each i in I intersect C. Choose one actual original anchor at each C type, and one actual original non-anchor donor x_i at each i in I. Such labels exist. All other original labels stay unchanged. Different choices give the same analytical construction.

A receiver w in N becomes activated when a donor is transferred to the full original star M_w. Exactly one additional label is retained there and is never moved again during the forward construction. A donor is used at most once. Every permitted transfer i->w requires iw in E(G) and a previously unactivated receiver w. Each transfer shrinks its donor from M_i to {iw}, then expands it to M_w; all deletions precede additions. A release deletes an unused donor's entire M_i and ends the construction at its first vacancy. This deliberately specified template does not include arbitrary partial-star interactions or return transfers.

## Saturated-neighbor activation closure

Starting R=empty, repeatedly add any w outside R for which some i in I has N_G(i) minus R = {w}. Let R* be the resulting least fixed point, equivalently the least set closed under all implications N_G(i) minus {w} subset R => w in R for i in I and w in N_G(i). Define Z(R)={i in I:N_G(i) subset R}.

**Candidate theorem.** A first vacancy is reachable by this monotone full-star activation template iff |Z(R*)|>|R*|. Every positive instance admits unchanged actual C anchors, all original floors, original domination and uniform safety for every original protected hidden completion. The closure and the criterion are independent of rule order. This is an exact classification of the template, only a sufficient criterion for unrestricted native reachability.

## Construction and safety

Track activated receivers R and used donors J, with a bijection from J to R recording transfers. Initially both empty. At macro boundaries each used donor occupies its assigned full receiver star; each unused donor remains original. Thus counts are a-1_J+1_R. Every used donor has all saturated neighbors in R.

If unused i has N_G(i) subset R, release x_i. Every original saturated loss at iw is compensated by the extra full receiver label at w. Nonsaturated floors and upper-four follow from the unchanged actual C anchors. Domination holds during deletion. Other labels are nonempty; the final deletion is the first vacancy.

Otherwise choose unused i with N_G(i) minus R={w}. Shrink x_i to iw. Every other saturated root incident to i has its extra receiver support already present. Root iw retains x_i through the entire transfer. Expand to M_w, creating a new extra receiver label; no floor is decreased by expansion. All nonsaturated roots and upper-four are protected by the unchanged C anchors. The donor remains nonempty throughout. Since w is new, this extends the J-to-R bijection. The root iw exists in H because it is saturated. No source type is invented or missing from the original source; current counts may become zero at non-anchor donor types.

Every slice is dominated by original stars. If a protected full system acquired a two-label cover, replacing current core labels by their original containing stars would contradict original lower-three protection. The unchanged C anchors supply upper-four independently of hidden incidences. This establishes universal safety, not observation or actual-successor enforcement.

## Closure, exactness and order

The implication operator is monotone on finite receiver sets, so asynchronous saturation reaches its unique least fixed point R*. A donor that has fired has all its neighbors activated thereafter and can never fire again. Hence a closure run realizes an injective assignment of one distinct donor to every activated receiver, and J subset Z(R), |J|=|R|.

If no unused zero-neighbor donor exists, every member of Z(R) is used. If R is not closed, any applicable donor with exactly one missing neighbor cannot already be used, so the next closure rule is realizable as a safe transfer. Therefore either a release becomes available, or one reaches R*. At R*, an unused releasable donor exists exactly when |Z(R*)|>|R*|.

An early release also implies the final inequality. Under a subsequent closure rule adding one receiver, its firing donor was not in Z(R) and newly enters Z; hence |Z(R)|-|R| never decreases. Thus an early positive surplus persists to R*. Conversely if final surplus is positive, executing closure transfers without releasing early leaves an unused donor in Z(R*) that can be deleted. Necessity applies only to the defined template: a transfer to a new receiver must leave all other saturated neighbors already compensated, since its full-star donor loses those incidences and no other labels have changed except previous completed receiver transfers. A release similarly requires all its saturated neighbors activated. No arbitrary-native-path normalization is asserted.

## Reversal and costs

The reverse of any constructed route restores the exact original labelled source, provided the reserve and all other labels have not been altered in between. Every reversed state is one of the already safe forward states. This is an exact release-and-reversal construction, not permission to insert arbitrary repair in the middle, nor a general exchange/restoration theorem.

A transfer i->w costs deg_H(i)+deg_H(w)-2 actual edits; release of t costs deg_H(t). The retained saturated edge prevents early emptiness. The constructed cost is the sum over chosen transfers plus final release; no shortest-path claim. Equal stars in a K2 component need care: the prospective anchor eligibility and fixed cover exclude using its two singleton endpoints as an unprotected reserve; the formula can give a zero-edit relabelling of its container. Such a macro changes the bookkeeping assignment, not the actual state. It must not be counted as a committed incidence edit or a source escape. The canonical certificate must explicitly retain this distinction.

## Hand-derived controls

On H=K_{4,3} with I={0,1,2,3}, N={4,5,6}, original anchors C={4,5,6}, all multiplicities one, take saturated edges 04,14,15,25,26,36. Activate 4 using donor0, then5 using donor1, then6 using donor2, and release donor3. There is no original saturated cherry: the degree-one donors have different neighbors. This yields three genuine cross-star transfers and a first vacancy in18 actual edits (each transfer costs5, release costs3), with three original anchors unchanged. It generalizes the one-step cherry mechanism to a compensation chain.

On the same carrier with G=H, closure is empty and Z(empty) is empty: the donor deficiency4>3 gives a static reserve but no template release. All saturated degrees exceed one, so the inherited source-escape theorem also rules out unrestricted release here.

With G empty, any donor releases directly. A two-donor common-neighbor pattern recovers the inherited cherry construction as a special case, without claiming a new five-type result. Fixed-cover eligibility remains essential; an unanchored numerical success cannot establish the theorem for an excluded singleton donor.

## Open boundaries

The choice of I and C is supplied and exact. No assertion that every reachable reserve has such an activation witness. Native acquisition, retained record origin, enforcement, actual-successor selection, guaranteed progress, broad C3/C4-C6 and physical derivation remain OPEN. Optional NOOPs can stall forever. No new primitive, full-state sensor, hidden-dependent outcome, compulsory commitment, fundamental time, dark-matter variable or geometry is introduced. No numerical campaign has yet run.

# Independent analytical review: reserve activation

Verdict: **ACCEPT for the declared saturated-neighbor monotone activation template**, with one nonblocking domain clarification below. No mathematical counterexample found. This is a raw analytical review, not a numerical or implementation verification and not an unrestricted native-reachability result.

Reviewed `RESULT.md` against the source-escape result and closeout retained in `source_readbacks.json`, parent `c31f5313486be2be25ff1d32d01b507d2de2e313`. No enumeration was run; no proof or implementation file was modified.

## Criterion, assignment, and order

The finite Horn closure is well defined and independent of fair exhaustive rule order. In a run adding one new receiver w at a time, a firing donor i becomes a member of Z immediately. That donor cannot fire again: its entire saturated neighborhood stays activated. Consequently each added receiver has a distinct donor, and a full run constructs the claimed injection J -> R* with |J|=|R*|. The assigned objects can be actual preselected original labels, not merely type counts.

Each activation adds at least its firing donor to Z while adding one receiver, so |Z(R)|-|R| never decreases. The difference is nonnegative along a realizable closure run and counts exactly the unused releasable donors at its macro boundaries. Thus positive terminal surplus is sufficient; an earlier release-eligible donor implies the same positive terminal surplus. This also excludes dependence on an unlucky firing choice: every exhaustive order has the same final sets and leaves a donor available exactly under the stated strict inequality. The existence of saturated-degree-zero donors is handled correctly by Z(empty).

## Floor, cover, and label safety

Independence of I in G is substantive: a saturated root incident to a donor has its other endpoint outside I, so another donor never independently removes an original incidence at that same saturated root. At a transfer, every saturated edge lost before the pivot has an already retained full receiver label, and the pivot itself retains the moving label. A release uses the same compensation on all saturated neighbors. Original C anchors cover every H root throughout, giving both floor one for nonsaturated roots and an actual cover of at most four labels. Multiplicity at I intersect C supplies the distinct donor and anchor. Multiple choices of original copy yield the same argument without identifying distinct actual labels.

At every deletion slice the donor stays inside M_i; after the pivot it stays inside M_w. Other moving labels already occupy original full stars. Original-star domination therefore supports the inherited substitution proof of lower-three protection for every fixed original protected hidden completion. This establishes uniform admissibility, not an observation, enforcement, selection, or progress mechanism.

## Native edits, reversal, and equal stars

For distinct adjacent stars in a simple graph, their intersection is precisely the pivot edge. The transfer requires deg_H(i)-1 actual deletions and deg_H(w)-1 actual additions. The donor never becomes empty during such a transfer. A final release costs deg_H(t) and reaches its first vacancy on its last deletion. Reversing the actual edit sequence traverses exactly the safe forward states and restores the original labelled source when no intervening operation has changed it. No exchange theorem follows for use of the reserve between the two routes.

A saturated K2 component permits a zero-edit container reassignment because the two endpoint stars are equal. This does not introduce native motion or source escape. Since G-independence permits at most one donor endpoint on that saturated edge, that isolated component can contribute only one used donor and one receiver, hence no positive surplus. With singleton endpoints, C eligibility also prevents selecting the anchored endpoint as the donor. The bookkeeping event is safe, but should remain explicitly separate from actual committed edit records, as the candidate requires. Positive constructions elsewhere do not turn this isolated zero-edit event into an extra source escape.

## Hand-derived chain and novelty

The K_{4,3} fixture is sound. Its saturated subgraph is the alternating path 0-4-1-5-2-6-3. Its initial degree-one donor endpoints have distinct saturated neighbors, so it has no initial two-donor common-neighbor cherry. Donor 0 activates 4, enabling donor 1 to activate 5, enabling donor 2 to activate 6, after which donor 3 releases. Each donor star has degree three and each receiver star degree four. Each of the three transfers costs five actual edits and release costs three, for exactly eighteen constructed edits. The unchanged labels at 4, 5, and 6 give the fixed three-cover. All three transfers include genuine outside-original-star additions.

This is a substantive extension from the inherited one-step cherry: a closure of successive compensation events and an exact order-independent criterion for that specified template. It is not a new theorem about all native paths, shortest reserves, repair after reserve use, or native record origin. The G=H control has empty closure and no release; its failure is also independently explained by the inherited saturated-degree source lock. Empty G and the cherry specialization are correctly identified as inherited/simple controls rather than new classifications.

## Nonblocking clarification

State directly in Domain that a transfer i -> w uses **w in N_G(i) minus R** (a saturated pivot), if that is the intended template. The construction later says the pivot exists because it is saturated, but Domain currently only says receivers belong to N_G(I) and a donor shrinks to {iw}.

The broader literal reading could permit a nonsaturated H-edge pivot to a new receiver. Such a transfer can be safe only after all saturated neighbors of its donor are already in R, so a release is already available at its start. Therefore this ambiguity does not furnish a counterexample to the vacancy-existence criterion. However, a proof for that broader template should stop at the first release-eligible boundary: before it, every legal transfer necessarily uses a unique missing saturated neighbor and follows the closure. It should not imply that every permitted transfer in the broader reading is itself a closure firing. Tightening the domain is the cleaner choice for the candidate's stated scope.

## Remaining limits

This acceptance is analytical and scoped. It does not certify future enumeration completeness, canonical certificate construction, test coverage, publication provenance, native acquisition/access, enforcement, actual-successor choice, progress despite NOOPs, arbitrary repair/restoration, or broad C3/C4-C6 claims. The current candidate preserves these boundaries appropriately.

The recent admission and record-transfer results are useful conditional mathematics. They do not establish native acquisition of their inputs. The current proved chain begins with a correctly initialized and accessible global record:

global singleton/pair miss field -> outside-root singleton profile -> exact admission bit -> restricted safe repair policy.

The first arrow is the record-transfer identity; the next is the empty-intersection criterion. Their composition is valid WHEN the global field and template are supplied. The missing connection is from previously justified native input/update objects to an accessible retained field or another sufficient admission certificate. Global moments are one sufficient route, not a necessary representation of every possible solution.
